The Door

Jamaican cooking, served like fine dining.

One of the very few upscale Jamaican restaurants in New York City — a white-tablecloth dining room, a full bar, and the island classics done properly, at prices that stay reasonable.

— the room

A dining room, not a counter

White tablecloths, professional table service and reggae in the background — Jamaican food with the full sit-down treatment, plus a busy takeout counter when you're in a hurry.

— the table

Every entrée, the full welcome

Each entrée arrives with soup or salad and a warm bread basket — the way dinner here has always started.

— the week

Buffets worth planning around

Thursday brings the seafood & chicken buffet; Sunday morning is the breakfast buffet and brunch — including banana oatmeal porridge you won't find anywhere else nearby.

House signatures

The plates people cross Queens for

Slow-braised, fire-kissed and steamed to order — the dishes The Door is known for, plated with care.

Oxtail

Seasoned very well and always with lots of gravy — the plate regulars measure every other oxtail against.

$29.95

Jerk Chicken

Charred edges, deep spice and the house jerk sauce on the side — the one guests wish they could buy by the bottle.

$23.99

Steamed Red Snapper

Whole snapper steamed with okra, carrots and pumpkin — or take it brown-stewed, escovitched, or in coconut run-down.

$29.95

Curried Lobster

Lobster in a golden curry, or buttered — and for the table that wants it all, jerk steak & lobster.

Market price

Every week

Two standing invitations

The rituals that fill the room — reserve ahead, especially on Sundays.

Thursdays

Seafood & Chicken Buffet

The week's big spread — seafood and chicken, island-style, in the full dining room. Come hungry; the buffet is the best value in the house.

Call for Thursday details
Sunday mornings

Breakfast Buffet & Brunch

Ackee & saltfish, callaloo, waffles — and the banana oatmeal porridge guests drive across the borough for. Sunday at The Door starts early and easy.
